info.title: PrijsProfeet API
info.description:
Realtime supermarktaanbiedingen van 10 Nederlandse supermarkten, genormaliseerd naar één JSON-schema, plus cross-retailer prijsvergelijking. Exacte matching gaat op EAN. Niet elke keten publiceert die: levert `/match/*` geen EAN-match op, dan volgt een benadering op naam, merk en categorie (indicatief, geen productidentiteit). De actuele EAN-dekking per keten staat op [prijsprofeet.nl/api](https://www.prijsprofeet.nl/api#ean-dekking).

**Geen API-key nodig** voor de publieke endpoints (zoeken, productdetail, aanbiedingen, categorieën). Zonder key gelden limieten *per endpoint, per IP*: 120/min op zoeken en productdetail, 30/min op de lijst- en bulk-endpoints.

**Gratis key: 150/min op je key in plaats van je IP.** Zelf aan te vragen op [prijsprofeet.nl/api](https://www.prijsprofeet.nl/api#gratis-key) — mailadres, klik op de link, key. Bouw je server-side, dan deelt je hele gebruikersbestand anders één IP-limiet.

Een `X-API-Key` is *verplicht* voor cross-retailer EAN-matching (`/match/*`) en prijsgeschiedenis (`/price-history`). Die zitten in het Pro-plan — zie [prijsprofeet.nl/api](https://www.prijsprofeet.nl/api).

**Let op — de goedkoopste match is niet altijd te koop.** `/match/*` geeft ook acties terug die pas *volgende week* beginnen (ongeveer een kwart van de catalogus) en rijen met de prijs die een keten *recent* rekende. Dat is opzet — "volgende week bij Jumbo goedkoper" is precies wat je gebruiker wil weten. Maar een `min(price)` over alle matches levert dan een prijs op die vandaag niet bestaat. Elke match draagt `is_current_deal` (`true`/`false`), `promotion_status` (`active` | `upcoming` | `historical`) en `valid_from`/`valid_until`: filter of label daarop.

**Noem jezelf in je User-Agent.** Niet verplicht, wel netjes — en het is de enige manier waarop we je kunnen bereiken bij een breaking change. Conventie (zoals GitHub): `NaamVanJeApp/1.0 (+https://jouw-site.nl)` of `NaamVanJeApp/1.0 (jij@voorbeeld.nl)`.

**Let op — `bot` in je User-Agent.** Verzoeken *zonder* API-key waarvan de User-Agent `bot`, `crawler`, `spider` of `slurp` bevat krijgen een `403`. Dat is anti-scrapebescherming, geen storing. Kies een naam zonder die woorden — of pak een gratis key, dan geldt de blokkade niet.

Op elk gebruik van deze API — met of zonder key — zijn de [API-voorwaarden](https://www.prijsprofeet.nl/api-voorwaarden) van toepassing.

get.description: Health check endpoint - verifies all services are operational

List all products with optional filters and pagination.

- **retailer**: Filter by retailer name
- **folder_id**: Filter by folder ID
- **is_promotional**: Filter promotional products only
- **min_price**: Minimum price (inclusive)
- **max_price**: Maximum price (inclusive)
- **min_valid_from**: Only promotions starting on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- **max_valid_from**: Only promotions starting on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- **sort_by**: Sort field (extracted_at, price, name, product_id, valid_from)
- **sort_order**: Sort order (asc or desc)
- **page**: Page number (starts at 1)
- **page_size**: Number of items per page (max 100)

Search products by name.

- **query**: Search query (product name)

- **page**: Page number (starts at 1)
- **page_size**: Number of items per page (max 100)

Get all products from a specific folder.

- **folder_id**: Folder identifier

Get all products for a specific retailer.

- **retailer**: Retailer name (aldi, albert_heijn, jumbo)
- **page**: Page number (starts at 1)
- **page_size**: Number of items per page (max 100)

Get all promotional products, cheapest first.

- **retailer**: Optional retailer filter
- **page**: Page number (starts at 1)
- **page_size**: Number of items per page (max 100)

`total` is the number of promotions matching the filter, not the size of
this page: divide it by `page_size` to know how many pages to fetch. There
is no result cap — paging to the last page returns the whole set, and the
ordering is stable across pages, so a full walk yields every promotion once.

Search products using Elasticsearch with fuzzy matching.

All products are promotions (scraped from bonus/aanbieding pages).

Features:
- Fuzzy search (handles typos)
- Dutch language analysis
- Relevance scoring
- Fast performance
- Filter by promotion status (active/upcoming/expired)
- Filter by promotion type (percentage, multi_buy, one_plus_one, etc.)
- Filter by minimum savings percentage
- Sort by savings, unit price, or regular price
- Filter by unified category
- Filter by dietary tags (bio, glutenvrij, lactosevrij, vegan)

Example: `/api/v1/search?q=kaas&category=zuivel-eieren&promotion_status=active`
Example: `/api/v1/search?q=*&promotion_type=multi_buy&min_savings=20&sort_by=savings_percentage:desc`
Example: `/api/v1/search?q=melk&dietary=vegan,lactosevrij`

parameters.name: current_only

schema.description: Only return matches you can actually buy today (is_current_deal=true). Default false, so the response also carries promotions that start next week and prices a retailer charged recently — deliberate, but a min(price) over all of them returns a price that does not exist yet. Costs coverage: on our own comparison cards, dropping the non-current rows left 29% of products with no match at all.

get.description:
Get top promotional deals grouped by brand.

Returns two lists:
- **top_by_percentage**: Best deals by savings percentage (e.g., 50% off)
- **top_by_amount**: Best deals by absolute savings (e.g., save EUR 5.00)

Products are grouped by brand + promotion_type to avoid showing
15 variants of the same Calve sauce.

Pass **retailer** (repeatable) to scope the lists to the shops you actually
visit — e.g. only the three supermarkets on your street.

Each group carries a `representative_product` with `name`, `price`,
`original_price`, `savings_percentage`, `image_url`, `product_url` and
`valid_from`/`valid_until`. Cache the response by all means, but check
`valid_until` before you render it: promotion weeks roll over mid-week and a
cached deal can expire between two of your refreshes.

post.description:
Request a free API key. We mail a link; clicking it issues the key.

The response is deliberately the same whether or not the address already has
a key — otherwise this endpoint would answer "is X a customer of yours?" for
any X. The 5/hour cap is per IP and exists so nobody can use us to mail-bomb
a stranger's inbox.

ean.title: Ean
ean.description: EAN/GTIN barcode. Published by Albert Heijn, Jumbo and partly Ekoplaza; null for the other seven chains.

original_price.title: Original Price
original_price.description: Price before the promotion (the 'van' in van/voor)

retailer_category.title: Retailer Category
retailer_category.description: The category as the retailer itself publishes it, verbatim. Every chain has its own taxonomy, so these strings are NOT comparable across retailers — use unified_category for that. Albert Heijn publishes it as 'Hoofdcategorie/Subcategorie'. Null at Aldi, Hoogvliet and Vomar, which publish no category at all; Lidl publishes the single constant 'Food' on every product, so treat that as absent too.

unified_category.title: Unified Category
unified_category.description: One of the 18 unified category slugs. Derived: we take the retailer's own category where it is unambiguous and fall back to the product name otherwise — a normalisation across 10 chains, not the retailer's own taxonomy. Aldi, Hoogvliet and Vomar publish no category at all, so theirs is name-based.

dietary_tags.title: Dietary Tags
dietary_tags.description: bio | glutenvrij | lactosevrij | vegan | vegetarisch. Derived from product names and brand rules — indicative, not allergen information.

private_label.title: Private Label
private_label.description: Whether this is a retailer's own brand (huismerk)

nutriscore.title: Nutriscore
nutriscore.description: Nutri-Score grade a-e (lowercase). Albert Heijn only.

folder_id.title: Folder Id
folder_id.description: Associated folder ID (legacy, unused for scraped products)

retailer_preference.title: Retailer Preference
retailer_preference.description: The retailers a stored preference narrowed this search to, or null when nothing was narrowed. Set only for browser callers carrying a `pp_uid` cookie, and only when the preference actually excludes a retailer — always null for API-key callers.
